items.text: The US and China met to make trade deals, but the two countries failed to make a deal. In response, the US said that it would increase tariffs on billions of dollars of Chinese goods, and China said that it would also increase tariffs on about 60 billion dollars’ worth of US imports. The American stock market fell sharply as a result, with markets opening and closing in the red . President Trump said that the US needs to have a strong economy, and he will work with China when they meet again next month at the G-20 in Japan. Difficult words: tariff (a tax that people pay to buy or sell things between countries), in the red (below budget, without any money), G-20 (a meeting of the 20 largest governments and banks in the world). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The USA and China are trying to make trade deals, but they failed to do this. The USA said that it would raise tariffs on billions of dollars of Chinese imports . China said that it would also raise tariffs on about 60 billion dollars’ worth of US imports. The stock market fell quickly in response, and markets opened and closed with low numbers. President Trump said that the USA needs to have a strong economy and that he will work with China. They are going to meet again next month at G20, an important international meeting in Japan. Difficult words: tariff (a tax that you pay to buy or sell things between countries), import (things that you sell to another country), the stock market (a market where people buy and sell parts of companies; these parts are called stocks or shares). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The USA and China meet. They want to make trade deals . There are some problems. The USA says that it will make China pay more to sell things in the USA. China says that it will make the USA pay more to sell things in China. People do not like this. The stock market falls. President Trump says that the USA needs to be strong. It needs to make money. He wants to work with China. He is going to meet with China in Japan. Difficult words: trade deal (when countries decide how they will buy or sell things to each other), will (in the future), the stock market (a market where people buy and sell parts of businesses). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

To create plastic products, people combine the plastic with additives which make recycling difficult. Usually, people combine plastic products together and grind them up to make a new recycled plastic that is not easy to reuse. This is not very helpful for recycling. Berkeley Lab in California made a new type of plastic which solves this problem. The lab calls the new plastic PDK. When people put it into a high-acid solution , the plastic is separate from the other chemicals. Then people can truly recycle and reuse the plastic. The scientists hope that PDK will help keep plastics out of landfills and oceans. Difficult words: additive (a thing that people add/put in to help create something), grind (cut up in very tiny pieces) high-acid solution (a mixture with a lot of acid—acid helps to dissolve or break up things). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People make plastic products by mixing the plastic with additives . The additives make it difficult to recycle the plastic. To recycle plastic things, people grind them up first, but this new material is not easy to use again. A laboratory in California made a new type of plastic to deal with this problem. When scientists put the new plastic in a high-acid solution , the plastic and the additives break apart. People can then easily reuse the plastic. The scientists hope that this new plastic will help the planet and that there will be less plastic. Difficult words: additive (a thing that people add/put in to help make something), grind (cut up in very small pieces), high-acid solution (a mixture with a lot of acid—acid helps to break up things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People make plastic . To make it, they put in additives . It is easier to make plastic with additives. To recycle the plastic, people cut it into very small pieces. However, the plastic has the additives in it. The cut-up plastic is hard to use again. Scientists in California work on this problem. They make a new plastic. It can be recycled easily. The plastic and the additives can be broken apart easily. The scientists hope that this new plastic can help the planet. They want there to be less plastic. Difficult words: plastic (a material that people can turn into many types of things – bottles, phones, computers, bags), additive (a thing that people add/put in to help make something), recycle (turn something into a new thing to use it again). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Maryland, a small American state in the Mid-Atlantic region with a population of 6 million, raised the minimum age to buy tobacco and nicotine products from 18 to 21. The state’s governor said that it was a measure ‘to confront the sharp rise in teen vaping ’. According to one American agency, more than 2 million middle school and high school students used e-cigarettes in 2017. Maryland became the 13th US state to increase the tobacco sale age to 21. Last month, one senator said that he plans to put forward a law which would raise the tobacco sale age to 21 everywhere in the USA. Difficult words: measure (a method, a way), confront (deal with), vape (to smoke an e-cigarette or something similar). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Maryland is a small state in the USA in the Mid-Atlantic region and around 6 million people live there. Its governor raised the minimum age to buy tobacco and nicotine products from 18 to 21. He said that it is a reaction to the fact that so many teenagers are vaping . People say that more than 2 million middle school and high school students used e-cigarettes in 2017. Maryland is the 13th American state to raise the age from 18 to 21. One senator plans to make this raise everywhere in the USA. Difficult words: governor (the leader/boss of an American state), raise (make go up), vape (smoke an e-cigarette or something similar). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

‘Vaping’ is smoking e-cigarettes. In 2017 in the USA, 2 million children between 11–18 vape. Vaping is not healthy. You cannot buy cigarettes if you are 18 or younger. Some states raise this limit. In some states, you must be 21 to buy a cigar, a cigarette, or an e-cigarette. Maryland is a small state in the USA. It is in the Mid-Atlantic region. Around 6 million people live there. It is the 13th state that raises the limit to 21. Difficult words: raise (make go up). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Taiwan became the first Asian country to allow same-sex couples to marry. The country’s lawmakers approved this bill last Friday which goes into effect this Friday. Supporters of the change filled the streets of Taiwan, and the president tweeted that this law was a big step towards true equality, and it made Taiwan a better country. Difficult words: approve (say ‘yes’ to something), bill (a law). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Friday, Taiwan’s lawmakers approved a new law that lets men marry men and women marry women. Taiwan is the first Asian country where people can do this. Supporters of the law filled the streets of Taiwan. The country’s president tweeted that this was a big step towards true equality and that Taiwan became a better country. Difficult words: lawmaker (members of parliament/leader/bosses), approve (say ‘yes’ to something), supporter (a person who supports/likes something) equality (the idea that every person can do the same things). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a new law in Taiwan. Under this law, men can marry men. Women can marry women. Taiwan is the first Asian country where people can do this. Many people are happy about this new law. They come into the streets. The country’s president is happy, too. She tweets that this makes Taiwan a better country. Difficult words: law (a document which says what people can or cannot do), marry (become husbands or wives), tweet (say something on Twitter – an Internet website). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

According to the CDC (an American organisation concerned with health and safety), suicide is the second leading cause of death in young people in the USA. An American hospital carried out a nationwide study which looked at suicide rates of people aged 10–19 between 1975 and 2016. Suicide rates among young people have been on the rise for years, but it is growing faster among young girls. This data still shows that boys are more likely to kill themselves than girls, although starting in 2007, suicide rates for girls aged 10–14 went up by almost 13 per cent each year. Unfortunately, the study did not find out why more girls are killing themselves, but some think that the pressure of social media can be a factor. Difficult words: suicide (the act of killing yourself), suicide rate (how many people commit suicide). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the USA, suicide is the second most common cause of death in young people. Suicide rates of people aged 10–19 went up between 1975 and 2016. Young men are more likely to commit suicide than girls, but more girls are killing themselves. Every year from 2007, 13% more girls aged 10–14 committed suicide. The study does now know why more girls are killing themselves. Some people think that one reason is social media. Difficult words: suicide (the act of killing yourself), suicide rate (how many people commit suicide), commit suicide (kill yourself). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

This news is from the USA. It is about a problem. The problem is that young people commit suicide . Suicide is the second biggest killer of young people in the USA. People watch how many people commit suicide. The number of people goes up between 1975 and 2016. Boys commit suicide more than girls. However, this is changing. More and more girls are killing themselves. From 2007, more girls commit suicide every year. People do not know why. Some people say that more girls are committing suicide because of social media . Difficult words: commit suicide (kill yourself), social media (Internet websites like Instagram, Facebook and Twitter). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last August, people reported the virus of African Swine fever in China, but there have been 129 outbreaks in the country as of last week. By the end of the year, China expects to lose about one-third of its pigs – 1 million pigs have died so far. There is no vaccine or cure against the disease and once a pig catches it, it is going to die. Some pig farmers even had to slaughter their healthy pigs to stop the spread of the virus. The virus has already spread to Mongolia, Vietnam and Cambodia where around 95,000 pigs have died. China is the world’s largest pork producing country, and the massive hit to the pork industry is already creating a ripple effect worldwide. For example, the soy bean market expects to fall because farmers in China will not need as much for pig feed. Difficult words: outbreak (an epidemic, when a lot of people or animals get ill), cure (medicine that makes a disease or sickness stop), ripple effect (things which happen because/after something happens). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

China is the largest producer of pork , but it is having a big problem at the moment. There is an epidemic which is killing its pigs. Last August, people first discovered the virus in China, but 1 million pigs are dead now. The virus is deadly and when a pig catches it, it is going to die. China thinks that one third of its pigs are going to die by the end of this year. The virus also spread to Mongolia, Vietnam and Cambodia where around 95,000 pigs died. Difficult words: pork (pig meat), epidemic (when many people or animals get ill), spread (move, get). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China is the biggest producer of pork . China is having problems. Many Chinese pigs are ill. One million of them are dead. They are ill because they have a virus. The virus is deadly. If a pig catches it, it is going to die. By the end of this year, China will have only 66% of its pigs. Difficult words: producer (somebody which produces – makes, has), pork (pig meat), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 1989, developed nations adopted a plan called the Basel Convention to regulate sending their toxic waste to less developed countries. On Friday 10 th , they added a new agreement to the treaty. The agreement aims to limit pollution from plastic. There are 195 countries in the world and a total of 187 signed the new agreement and agreed to restrict plastic pollution. One of the bigger countries which did not sign was the USA. Although the US chose not to participate, the rules still apply when the country tries to move plastic waste to any of the 187 participating countries once the rules go into effect in a year. It has been common for companies to ship waste to less developed nations. For instance , China used to take in half of the world’s trash, but it stopped accepting a majority of it last year in an effort to curb pollution. Difficult words: developed (rich), instance (example), curb (limit). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The Basel Convention took effect in 1989, and it forbids developed countries to send their toxic waste to less developed countries. On Friday 10 th , 187 countries signed another agreement . The countries which signed agreed to limit plastic pollution . There are 195 countries in the world, and the USA was one of the countries which did not sign the agreement. Difficult words: developed (rich, with technology), agreement (a plan to which countries agree – say ‘yes’ to the plan), pollution (things which people throw away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Countries sign a new agreement . This agreement is about plastic pollution . The agreement limits plastic. There are 195 countries in the world. Almost every country signs the agreement. One hundred and eighty-seven countries sign it. The USA is one of the countries which does not sign. Difficult words: sign (say ‘yes’), agreement (a plan), pollution (things which people throw away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The centre-right opposition in Albania considers the current government corrupt and says that votes were stolen in the parliamentary elections. There have been protests in Albania for three months – the people demand that the socialist prime minister step down and that the parliament hold an election. Many opposition lawmakers even stepped down from parliament in protest. Large-scale protests last Saturday continued into Sunday and turned violent – people threw Molotov cocktails while police used tear gas and water cannons. The police arrested 50 people that weekend, and the organisers called for an even larger rally on Monday. The Albanian Prime Minister, Edi Rama, called the opposition’s stance ‘blind’. The American Embassy in Albania called for an end to the violence, saying that the opposition is working against its own goal because ‘violence is inherently undemocratic’. Difficult words: demand (to ask strongly), rally (a big meeting of protesters), inherently (characteristically, typically). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

People in Albania started protesting three months ago. They say that the government is corrupt and that their votes were stolen. They want the socialist prime minister to step down, and they want a new election . There were big protests last Saturday and Sunday. People threw Molotov cocktails, and the police used tear gas and water cannons. Police arrested fifty people that weekend. Difficult words: government (the leaders/bosses of a country), corrupt (corrupt politicians do not work to make their country better but to get rich or get power), election (a situation when people vote for/choose their leaders/bosses). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People in Albania protest. They protest against their government . They say that it is corrupt . The people want the prime minister to step down. They want a new election . There are big protests last Saturday and Sunday. People throw fire. The police fight back. They arrest 50 people. Difficult words: government (the leaders/bosses of a country), corrupt (a corrupt government does not help the people of a country, and it does bad things), election (when people vote for/choose their leaders/bosses). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Chris Hughes was a co-founder of Facebook, and he wrote in the New York Post that it is time for the company to break up. He said that Facebook and its CEO, Mark Zuckerberg, have far too much power beyond the private sector or the government. He added that Zuckerberg should regulate how giant Facebook has become, saying that although Zuckerberg is a good person, he sacrificed ‘security and civility for clicks’. Other people and groups are asking for more regulation over Facebook after its recent data privacy problems. Zuckerberg has admitted that he would be open to some control of the Internet – one which could preserve what is best about it while protecting people from harm . Difficult words: co-founder (someone who helps to found – start a company), civility (politeness, thinking about other people), harm (a bad effect or danger). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

A co-founder of Facebook wrote in a newspaper that is time for the company to break up. He said that Facebook and its CEO , Mark Zuckerberg, have too much power. However, he added that Zuckerberg is a good person, but he chose popularity and money over security and civility . Other people want the government to regulate Facebook after its recent problems, such as data privacy. Zuckerberg said that he would think about some control of his company. Difficult words: co-founder (someone who helps to found – start a company), CEO (boss; a chief executive officer), civility (thinking about other people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A co-founder of Facebook writes in a newspaper. He says that is time for the company to get smaller. He says that Facebook has too much power. He says that its boss, Mark Zuckerberg, has too much power, too. He says that Zuckerberg is a good man. However, he chooses money over safety. He lets Facebook get less and less safe. Facebook has problems. One of the problems is people’s privacy . Some people want the government to control Facebook. Zuckerberg says that this can happen. Difficult words: co-founder (someone who helps to found – start a company), privacy (if you have privacy on the Internet, nobody can see information about you), government (the bosses of a country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis signed a bill last Wednesday which will allow teachers to carry guns at school. After the law goes into effect on October 1st, school boards will still need to give authorisation to their teachers. Teachers who choose to arm themselves will need to undergo at least 144 hours of training and take psychological and drug tests. Difficult words: bill (a law), arm (get a gun). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last Wednesday, the governor of Florida signed a new law that goes into effect in October, and it lets teachers carry guns at school. Teachers who choose to carry a gun must undergo at least 144 hours of training and do psychological and drug tests. Also, each school will need to decide if it will let its teachers carry guns or not. Difficult words: sign (write your name to show that you are saying ‘yes’ to what is written in a document), undergo (do), decide (choose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

There is a new law in Florida. The governor of Florida signs it. The new law starts in October. The law says that teachers can have a gun at school. A teacher must be ready if he or she wants a gun. The teacher must do at least 144 hours of training. The teacher must also do drug tests and psychological tests. Also, every school can choose if its teachers can have guns. Difficult words: law (a document which says what people can and cannot do), governor (the leader/boss of an American state), sign (write your name to show that you are saying ‘yes’ to what is written in a document). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People import seventy per cent of Cuba’s food, and there has not been enough food in the country recently. Cuban citizens have been on a rationing system since 1959, but the government now imposed strict rationing on basic foods like chicken, eggs and rice. The Cuban government said that the new rationing system is necessary after the USA put more restrictions on the country. The relationship between Cuba and the USA is not good because each country supports a different leader in Venezuela. Cuba has close ties to Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro while the USA strongly backs his opponent, Juan Guaidó. The USA also said that it would put a complete embargo on Cuba if Cuba did not send away its soldiers in Venezuela, but Cuba said that there were no Cuban soldiers there. Difficult words: rationing system (a system when each person gets a little food), impose (set, put), embargo (ban/stop imports and exports). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Cuba does not produce enough food for its people, and it imports 70% of food. A rationing system started in 1959 and people still use it. Now, the Cuban government put even more rationing into place. Food like chicken, eggs and rice are given to each person in small amounts. Cuba says that it has to do this because of American restrictions . The relationship between Cuba and the USA is not good. Cuba supports Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro, but the USA supports his opponent, Juan Guaidó. The USA also says that Cuba has soldiers in Venezuela. It says that if Cuba does not tell the soldiers to go away, it will put a complete embargo on Cuba. On the other hand, Cuba says that there are no Cuban soldiers in Venezuela. Difficult words: rationing system (a system when each person gets a little food), restriction (limits, stopping something), embargo (stop imports and exports). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Cuba does not produce enough food. People must import food to Cuba. This is a problem. There is never enough food in Cuba. People cannot buy as much food as they want. Each person can buy only a little food. This is for normal food like chicken, eggs and rice. The situation is worse now in Cuba. Cuba says that this is because of the USA. Cuba says that the USA is blocking Cuba. There are political problems in Venezuela at the moment. Cuba likes the leader there. The USA likes a second leader. The USA wants Cuba to stop liking the other leader. Also, the USA says that Cuba has soldiers in Venezuela. The USA says that Cuba must send the soldiers away. Cuba says that there are no Cuban soldiers in Venezuela. Difficult words: produce (make), import (bring from another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Researchers conducted a study on global alcohol consumption and found that it is rising. The researchers carried the study out between 1990 and 2017, and they focused on the annual amount of alcohol consumed per person over 15 years old. In 1990, the average person consumed 5.9 litres of pure alcohol and in 2017, consumed 6.5 litres. This amount of alcohol translates to a little more than one drink a day. If alcohol consumption rises, the average person will have just over eight drinks a week. Not only are people drinking more per person, but more people are drinking. Around 45% of people drank in 1990, a number that rose to 47% in 2017 and can rise to 50% in 2030. Alcohol consumption can be a big health problem. The World Health Organisation reports that 3 million people die because of alcohol every year, and alcohol plays a big role in over 200 diseases. The authors of the study say that the rise in alcohol consumption comes from a rise of wealth . The largest rise in wealth happened in India and Vietnam. Difficult words: annual (yearly), pure alcohol (only alcohol, not an alcoholic drink), wealth (the money that people have). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Scientists study how much people drink between 1990 and 2017. The study is global, and it includes everyone older than 15. In 1990, the average person drank 5.9 litres of pure alcohol per year. In 2017, the number was up to 6.5 litres a year. For 2017, such amount of alcohol is a drink every day. If this trend continues, the average person will drink eight drinks a week. Not only are people drinking more, more people are drinking, too. Around 45% of people drank in 1990, and 47% of people drank in 2017. This can rise to 50% by 2030. Drinking alcohol can be dangerous. The World Health Organisation says that 3 million people die because of alcohol every year. Difficult words: global (about the whole world), the average person (‘typical’ or ‘usual’), pure alcohol (only alcohol, not an alcoholic drink). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Scientists watch how much people drink. They start watching in 1990. In 1990, the typical person drinks 5.9 litres of alcohol a year. That is around one drink a day. In 1990, 45% of people drink. In 2017, people drink more. They drink 6.5 litres a year. That is more than in 1990. That is around eight drinks a week. More people drink, too. Around 47% of people drink in 2017. In 2030, it is possible that 50% of people will drink. People are drinking more. More people are drinking. Alcohol can be dangerous. Scientists say that 3 million people die because of alcohol every year. Difficult words: scientists (an expert, somebody who works at university), it is possible (it can happen), will (in the future). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prince Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, introduced their son Archie to the world last Wednesday. His full name is Archie Harrison Mountbatten-Windsor. The media has not yet found a connection either between Prince Harry’s or Meghan’s families and the name Archie. They say that the name can mean ‘brave’, ‘ bold ’ or ‘ genuine ’, so it may be fitting to be simply the baby’s own name. Harrison probably means ’son of Harry’ and Mountbatten-Windsor is the surname which was created when Archie’s great-grandparents, Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, married in 1960. Harry and Meghan have broken some royal traditions – for example, they chose to keep their family affairs private, did not give their son a courtesy title , or posed for photographs a few days after the baby was born. Difficult words: bold (not afraid, brave), genuine (real, authentic), courtesy title (a title given because of tradition or respect, not a title which gives the child real power). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Prince Harry and Meghan showed the world their son Archie last Wednesday. His full name is Archie Harrison Mountbatten-Windsor. He is a famous royal baby; people analyse his name. They do not find any connection between Harry’s or Meghan’s families and the name ‘Archie’. ‘Archie’ can mean ‘ brave ’ or ‘ genuine ’. Harrison probably means ‘son of Harry’. ‘Mountbatten-Windsor’ was created in 1960 when Archie’s great-grandparents, Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip, married. Harry and Meghan are not doing everything traditionally. For example, they do not let people take photographs right after Archie was born. They wait a few days. Difficult words: connection (when two things have something in common, are similar or mean something), brave (unafraid), genuine (real, authentic). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Prince Harry and Meghan have a baby. He is a boy. His name is Archie. They show him to the world. Archie’s full name is Archie Harrison Mountbatten-Windsor. People want to know what his name means. ‘Archie’ means ‘ brave ’ or ‘ genuine ’. Harrison means ’son of Harry’. ‘Mountbatten-Windsor’ is a combination of names. ‘Mountbatten’ is the name of Prince Philip’s family. ‘Windsor’ is the name of the Queen’s family. ‘Prince Philip is Archie’s great-grandfather and the Queens’ husband. Difficult words: brave (not afraid), genuine (real), combination (a thing which is two or more things put together). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has been in power for 16 years, and his party dominated Turkey for even longer. However, the country’s economy has not been doing well under Erdogan and his popularity is suffering. Turkey held local elections on March 31st in which Erdogan’s party won across the nation, except in Istanbul, the largest city, and Ankara, the country’s capital. Such a situation is a major setback for Erdogan. Erdogan’s party requested a new election in Istanbul, saying that fraud influenced the results. The country’s Supreme Election Board agreed, and this final decision cannot be challenged in court. People planned the new local election in Istanbul for June. Erdogan said that the new election is an important step for Turkish democracy. On the other hand, the European Parliament said that a second vote would ruin the credibility of democratic Turkish elections. Difficult words: fraud (cheating, doing something illegal), influence (change), credibility (the fact that you can trust the election). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

This year is Erdogan’s 16th as president of Turkey. However, the country’s economy is not doing well, and he is becoming less popular. In March, there were local elections in Turkey. Erdogan’s party won all of Turkey except for two important cities – Istanbul, the largest city, and Ankara, the capital. Losing in these cities was not good for Erdogan. His party requested a new election in Istanbul – it said that there was fraud . The government accepted the request, and now it is planning a new election for June. Erdogan said that the new election is an important step for Turkish democracy. On the other hand, the European Parliament believes the opposite. Difficult words: local election (when people vote/choose their local leaders), request (formally asking for something), fraud (cheating, doing something illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Erdogan is the president of Turkey. This year is his 16th as president. He is popular. However, he is becoming less and less popular. In March, there are local elections in Turkey. People can choose people from Erdogan’s party . They can also choose people from another party. Erdogan’s party wins in almost all of Turkey. It does not win in two cities. These cities are Istanbul and Ankara. They are important. Istanbul is Turkey’s biggest city. Ankara is the capital. This is not good for Erdogan. He wants to change this. His party says that there is fraud in the election. It wants a new election in Istanbul. The party plans the new election for June. Erdogan is happy. He says that this is good for democracy. The European Parliament does not think so. It thinks that this is bad for democracy. Difficult words: local election (when people vote/choose their local leaders), party (a group of people who are in politics), fraud (cheating, something wrong/illegal). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Last Tuesday, Myanmar’s president, Win Myint, released more than 6,500 prisoners and granted them amnesty . People confirmed that among those pardoned were Reuters journalists Wa Lone and Kyaw Soe Oo. Before police arrested them in 2017, they were investigating the killings of Rohingya Muslims by Myanmar’s government. Later, police convicted them to seven years in prison. The United Nations applauded the journalists’ release, saying that it shows that the Myanmarese government wants a transition to democracy. Difficult words: amnesty (an official pardon), applaud (show that you are happy about something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Myanmar’s president pardoned more than 6,500 prisoners last Tuesday and set them free. Two Reuters journalists were among them. Police arrested the journalists and sent them to prison for seven years in 2017 for investigating the killings of Rohingya Muslims by Myanmar. The United Nations applauded the journalists’ release . The UN said that this shows that the Myanmarese government wants change into a democratic country. Difficult words: pardon (set someone free), applaud (show that you are happy about something), release (setting someone free). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Two journalist work for Reuters. They investigate the Myanmar government . They want to know if Myanmar killed Rohingya Muslims. Police arrest the journalists in 2017. They go to prison. They must be there for seven years. Last Tuesday, the president of Myanmar sets the journalists free. He sets free more than 6,500 prisoners, too. This is called an amnesty. The United Nations is happy that the president does this. Difficult words: investigate (get information), government (the bosses of a country), killed (past of ‘kill’). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In 2010 in the USA, a BP oil rig exploded, killing 11 people and leaking four million barrels of oil into the sea. In response, President Obama created stricter oil drilling regulations . Last week, the Trump Administration announced that it would roll back about 20% of those oil drilling laws, and the changes would take place in two months. It wants to focus on ‘smarter regulations’ that improve America’s energy, economy, and safety. One of the controversial changes is to allow oil rig operators to hire any inspectors that they want to check their safety equipment instead of only government inspectors. Some public comments were against the changes, but the administration said that the original rules did not help safety and were too expensive. Difficult words: oil rig (an installation that drills oil out in the ocean), regulation (a law or a rule that a government puts into place), controversial (making some people want to argue about it). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2010 in the USA, a BP oil rig exploded, which killed 11 people and leaked four million barrels of oil into the ocean. In response, President Obama created stronger oil drilling laws. Last week, the Trump Administration said that it plans to roll back some of those oil drilling laws, and it wants the changes to happen in two months. It wants ‘smarter’ laws that improve America’s energy, economy, and safety. Some people were against these changes, but the administration said that the old rules did not help safety and were too expensive. Difficult words: oil rig (a building that people put in the ocean to drill oil), administration (the people and groups who work for a person), roll back (start over, change). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Peter Mayhew died at age 74; he was the actor of the original Chewbacca in the ‘Star Wars’ films. Mayhew was about 221 centimetres tall from a genetic disorder called Marfan Syndrome that caused him to grow so tall. It helped him play the iconic role in the first ‘Star Wars’ film, ‘Episode III’ and ‘Star Wars: The Force Awakens’. His family announced the death on Twitter and wrote that ‘he put his heart and soul in the role’ and ‘the Star Wars family meant so much’. His co-star, Mark Hammill, also wrote on Twitter that he was ‘a big man with an even bigger heart’. Difficult words: genetic disorder (when your body develops in an unexpected way), iconic (well-known, famous, recognisable). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Powerful cyclone Fani made landfall in the state of Odisha in India around 8 a.m. local time last Friday. It brought heavy rain and wind speeds of more than 193 kilometres per hour. It is the strongest cyclone to have hit India in decades, and at least three people were reported dead on Friday. Around 1.2 million people were ordered to evacuate Odisha and moved into thousands of shelters . Classes at schools cancelled and airports shut down. The cyclone weakened slightly as it made landfall, and meteorologists predict that it will continue to weaken as it moves towards Bangladesh. Difficult words: make landfall (come to land from sea), shelter (a safe place), predict (say what you think is going to happen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Jakarta, which is home to more than 10 million people, is Indonesia’s capital on the island of Java. However, Indonesia’s planning minister recently said that President Joko Widodo has decided to relocate the capital to a new city outside of Java. The future capital is yet to be formally picked, but the city of Palangkaraya on the island of Borneo is a frontrunner . The main reason for the big move is Jakarta’s overpopulation. It is one of the most congested places in the world. The planning minister estimated that the city’s traffic jams cost the economy more than $7 billion a year. Also, Jakarta is one of the fastest-sinking cities in the world – one half of the city lays below sea level. Difficult words: frontrunner (the one that is likely to win), congested (overcrowded, with too many people), estimate (calculate). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Russian President Vladimir Putin signed a new measure last Wednesday which aims to create the country’s own Internet. This would mean that the Internet would no longer need to go through international servers. The change would let the government take control ‘in case there are threats to the stable, safe and integral operation of the Russian Internet’ in ‘Russian territory’. The country is expected to test the new system later this year, and the legislation is set to take effect in November. However, some critics fear the new measure could lead to censorship, as Newsy has previously reported. The new legislation might lead to Russia creating its own version of China’s Great Firewall, which China uses to severely hinder free speech. People reported that Russia has tried to suppress freedom in the past, namely by banning certain sites and messaging platforms because they refused to follow government orders to curb user privacy. Blogs with more than 3,000 monthly visitors have to be registered as media outlets since 2014. Difficult words: hinder (stop, block), suppress (make less, stop), curb (limit). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Russia plans to test this new system later this year and the laws will take effect in November. However, there are critics of the new system – they that say this could lead to censorship . Difficult words: censorship (stopping some information), firewall (a part of a computer system which blocks something), hinder (stop, block). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
